It explicitly calls `with_generic_param_rib`, `with_self_rib`, `with_lifetime_rib`, `with_optional_trait_ref`, `resolve_doc_links`, `walk_trait_ref`, `visit_ty`, `visit_generics`, `with_current_self_type`, `with_self_rib_ns`, and `resolve_impl_item`.

Resolves an associated item inside an impl, enforcing trait-membership checks when the impl targets a trait and using item-specific generic/lifetime scopes. It explicitly calls `resolve_doc_links`; for associated consts it calls `with_generic_param_rib`, `with_lifetime_rib`, `check_trait_item`, `visit_generics`, `visit_ty`, and `resolve_const_body`; for methods and associated types it uses `with_generic_param_rib`, `check_trait_item`, and `visit::walk_assoc_item`; and for delegations it calls `resolve_delegation`.

Validates that an impl associated item corresponds to an item in the currently referenced trait, records its resolution and visibility, reports missing or duplicate matches, and checks namespace/kind consistency. It explicitly calls `find_similarly_named_assoc_item` to build diagnostics, `report_error` to emit trait-membership errors, and `record_partial_res` to store the resolved trait item.

Resolves a constant expression body under elided-lifetime inference and const-context scoping. It explicitly calls `with_lifetime_rib`, `with_constant_rib`, and then `visit_expr` on the body expression.

Resolves a delegation item by resolving its path, optional qualified self type, and optional synthesized body scope. It explicitly calls `smart_resolve_path`, `visit_ty` for `qself`, `visit_path`, `fresh_binding` to introduce the implicit `self` binding, and `visit_block` for the body.

Resolves function parameters by first resolving parameter patterns under an elided-lifetime rib and then resolving each parameter type. It explicitly calls `with_lifetime_rib`, `resolve_pattern`, and `visit_ty`.
Resolves a local `let` binding by visiting its optional type, initializer, optional `else` block, and finally its pattern. It explicitly calls `visit_expr`, `visit_block`, and `resolve_pattern_top`.

Builds the binding map for a pattern while detecting never-pattern usage and recursively validating nested or-patterns. Checks whether a pattern node’s already-recorded base resolution is a local binding by reading `partial_res_map` and testing for `Res::Local`.

Computes and validates the combined binding map for an or-pattern, ignoring never arms, and reports missing bindings or inconsistent binding modes across alternatives. It explicitly calls `compute_and_check_binding_map` for each subpattern and `report_error` for `VariableNotBoundInPattern` and `VariableBoundWithDifferentMode` diagnostics.

Quickly scans a pattern for or-pattern or never-pattern structure and, if found, triggers full binding-consistency checking. It explicitly calls `compute_and_check_binding_map` when deeper validation is needed.
Resolves a match arm inside a fresh value rib, including its pattern, optional guard, and body. It explicitly calls `with_rib` and `resolve_pattern_top`.
Creates the top-level binding context for a pattern and resolves it. It explicitly calls `resolve_pattern`.

Resolves a pattern in three ordered phases: first walks the pattern with `walk_pat` so literals and substructure are seen before bindings are introduced, then delegates binding/path resolution to `resolve_pattern_inner`, and finally calls `check_consistent_bindings` to validate variant/binding consistency after resolution.

Performs the direct resolution work for each subpattern by walking it recursively, resolving identifier patterns as existing non-bindings via `try_resolve_as_non_binding` or creating new locals via `fresh_binding`, recording partial results, and resolving tuple-struct/path/struct patterns through `smart_resolve_path`; it also manages temporary binding contexts for or-pattern branches.

Creates or reuses a local pattern binding after normalizing the identifier, detecting duplicate bindings across product and or-pattern contexts, reporting duplicate-binding diagnostics through `report_error`, and accessing the current scope via `innermost_rib_bindings` to either reuse an existing or-pattern binding or insert a fresh `Res::Local`.
Returns the mutable binding map for the innermost rib of the requested namespace.

Attempts to interpret an identifier pattern as an already-existing value-space entity instead of a fresh binding by querying `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`, preserving usable constant/unit-ctor resolutions in syntactically ambiguous cases, recording uses when needed, and emitting shadowing/invalid-pattern diagnostics through `report_error` for resolutions that should not be silently rebound.
Convenience wrapper that resolves an AST path by converting it to segments and delegating to `smart_resolve_path_fragment` with finalization and partial-resolution recording enabled.

Core path-resolution routine that selects the namespace from the path source, resolves the path while handling qself/type-relative cases, defers or records partial results, and synthesizes rich use-site diagnostics; within this logic it calls `should_report_errs`, `smart_resolve_report_errors`, `suggest_adding_generic_parameter`, `append_result`, and `resolve_qpath_anywhere`.
Helper that merges a successful `Vec` result into another by appending with `append`, or propagates the first encountered error.
Checks whether `Self` is currently resolvable in the type namespace by calling `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope` on `Self` and rejecting `Res::Err`.
Checks whether `self` is currently resolvable in the value namespace by calling `maybe_resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope` on a span-tagged `self` identifier and rejecting `Res::Err`.
Reports a resolution error to the underlying resolver only when `should_report_errs` allows diagnostics in the current context.
Returns whether late resolution should emit diagnostics, suppressing them inside rustdoc function bodies and after a global resolution error already exists.

Tries to resolve a qualified path across multiple namespaces by repeatedly calling `resolve_qpath` for the primary, type, and value namespaces, and if unresolved and not type-qualified, falls back to macro lookup before returning the best partial result.

Resolves a possibly type-qualified path, handling `<T>::...` and `<T as Trait>::...` forms specially by calling `smart_resolve_path_fragment` to validate the trait and trait-item prefixes, then producing a partial result that leaves remaining associated segments for type checking or delegates normal path lookup to the lower-level resolver.

Executes a closure in a scope where an optional loop/block label has been registered: it tracks unused labels, checks for prior definitions via `resolve_label`, emits shadowing diagnostics, and introduces the binding with `with_label_rib` before invoking the closure.
Resolves a labeled block by wrapping `visit_block` inside `with_resolved_label` so the block body sees the label binding.

Resolves a block by pushing the appropriate value/type ribs for anonymous modules or normal lexical scope, tracking macro-definition ribs for nested `macro_rules!`, adjusting bare-struct-literal diagnostic state, visiting each statement with `visit_stmt`, and then restoring the prior module and rib stacks.
Resolves an anonymous constant by delegating to `resolve_anon_const_manual`, passing whether the expression is a trivial const argument and resolving the body expression through `resolve_expr`.

Sets up the scope rules for an anonymous constant based on its kind and generic-usage permissions, then resolves its body inside a constant rib and an elided-lifetime rib by calling `with_constant_rib`, `with_lifetime_rib`, and finally the supplied `resolve_expr` closure.
Resolves a struct expression field by resolving the field value with `resolve_expr`, visiting the field identifier with `visit_ident`, and then walking its attributes.

Main expression resolver that first calls `record_candidate_traits_for_expr_if_necessary`, then dispatches by expression kind to resolve paths with `smart_resolve_path`, labels with `resolve_label` and `report_error`, patterns with `resolve_pattern_top`, labeled constructs with `resolve_labeled_block` or `with_resolved_label`, nested blocks with `visit_block`, subexpressions with `resolve_expr`/`visit_expr`, path segments with `visit_path_segment`, and const arguments with `resolve_anon_const_manual`.

Precomputes trait candidates for field and method-call expressions by calling `traits_in_scope` on the accessed name and storing the resulting candidates for later diagnostics and method lookup assistance.
Queries the resolver for traits visible from the current scope and hygiene context that define the given name in the given namespace.
Collects visible lifetime bindings from the current lifetime-rib stack, including earlier synthesized anonymous-lifetime parameters when needed, and stores them for the specified `impl Trait` node.

Resolves a rustdoc link path in a namespace using a per-module cache, delegating cache misses to `resolve_rustdoc_path` and suppressing non-local results that cannot safely be encoded for proc-macro metadata.

Processes doc attributes when configured to do so, resolves each referenced path across namespaces by calling `resolve_and_cache_rustdoc_path`, resolves prefixes for associated-item or diagnostic support, and when needed records trait candidates for doc-link lookup via `traits_in_scope`.

Detects paths whose leading qualification is unnecessary by comparing recorded partial resolutions against direct lexical-scope lookup with `resolve_ident_in_lexical_scope`, and records a lint candidate when the unqualified form resolves identically.
Extracts a function signature’s delegation-relevant shape—header, parameter count, self receiver, and variadic flag—and stores it for the function’s local definition id.

Collects per-item metadata during AST traversal: for items with generics it counts lifetime parameters and stores the count, and for function items it additionally calls `collect_fn_info`; afterward it continues traversal with `walk_item`.
Collects signature metadata for associated functions by calling `collect_fn_info` when the associated item is a function, then continues traversal with `walk_assoc_item`.

Drives the crate-level late name-resolution pass: it first calls `visit::walk_crate` with `ItemInfoCollector` to gather item information, then calls `LateResolutionVisitor::new` to create the main resolver visitor, calls `resolve_doc_links` to resolve crate attribute doc links, calls `visit::walk_crate` again to traverse the expanded crate for late resolution, and finally iterates over collected unused labels and calls `buffer_lint` to emit `UNUSED_LABELS` lints.

Returns the underlying `DefId` for early-bound, late-bound, and free resolved arguments, and `None` for `StaticLifetime` or `Error`; it does not call other methods from the list.

Walks outward through the current scope stack to determine the binder variables and binder composition mode for a nested poly-trait-ref, including concatenating enclosing binder vars with supertrait vars when needed. Returns the HIR map used for nested visiting; it calls `hir` on the type context.
Visits a nested body within a `Body` scope so inner references resolve with the body boundary in place. It calls `hir`, `body`, `with`, `id`, and `visit_body`.

Handles closure expressions specially: it diagnoses inferred types inside `for<>` closures, builds late-bound vars for closure binders, rejects non-region late-bound params, records the binders, and then visits the closure within a new binder scope; non-closure expressions are walked normally. Local helper for `visit_expr` that searches a type for an inferred `_` and returns its span if found. It calls the nested visitor's `visit_ty` and then `break_value` on the control-flow result.
Searches a type subtree for the first inferred type and stores its span, otherwise continues traversal. It calls `is_some` to stop after a hit and `walk_ty` to recurse into nested types.

Dispatches item handling based on item kind: records empty late-bound vars for trait impl refs, uses `visit_early_late` for functions, walks items with no lifetime parameters directly, gives opaque types a parent-aware root plus binder and trait-ref-boundary scopes, and uses early-binding handling for other generic items. It calls `record_late_bound_vars`, `visit_early_late`, `walk_item`, `ResolvedArg::early`, `insert`, `with`, and `visit_early`.
Handles foreign items by using `visit_early_late` for foreign functions and otherwise just walking foreign statics and types. It calls `visit_early_late` and `walk_foreign_item`.

Resolves bindings inside types, with special handling for bare function types, trait objects, explicit lifetime parameters, references, and opaque defs. It builds and records late-bound vars for bare fns, visits trait-object bounds under a trait-ref boundary, applies object lifetime defaulting or normal lifetime visiting, and performs additional opaque-type validation. It calls `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `deny_non_region_late_bound`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, `walk_ty`, `visit_poly_trait_ref_inner`, `resolve_object_lifetime_default`, and `visit_lifetime`.

Handles trait items by using `visit_early_late` for methods, `visit_early` plus explicit traversal for associated types, and `visit_early` plus normal walking for associated consts. It calls `visit_early_late`, `walk_trait_item`, `visit_early`, `visit_generics`, `visit_param_bound`, and `visit_ty`.

Handles impl items by using `visit_early_late` for methods, `visit_early` plus explicit traversal for associated types, and `visit_early` plus normal walking for associated consts. It calls `visit_early_late`, `walk_impl_item`, `visit_early`, `visit_generics`, and `visit_ty`.

Resolves a lifetime reference according to its kind: inserts `'static`, resolves named lifetime params, and ignores error or inference/default placeholders for later stages. It calls `insert_lifetime` for `Static` and `resolve_lifetime_ref` for `Param`.

Visits each path segment's generic arguments with the correct depth and resolves paths that refer to type or const parameters. It calls `visit_segment_args` for segment arguments and `resolve_type_ref` on type/const parameter paths.

Processes a function-like item by extracting the output type, copying inferred-delegation late-bound vars when present, applying lifetime elision analysis, walking the function signature/kind, and then visiting the body. It calls `fn_sig`, `skip_binder`, `bound_vars`, `local_def_id_to_hir_id`, `visit_fn_like_elision`, `walk_fn_kind`, and `visit_nested_body`.
Visits generic parameters and where predicates inside a trait-ref-boundary scope so nested trait refs are resolved with the proper boundary. It calls `with`.

Resolves where-predicates by creating a binder scope for bound predicates, recording their late-bound vars, and then visiting the bounded type and bounds; region predicates visit the lifetime and bounds, while equality predicates visit both sides. It calls `ResolvedArg::late`, `late_arg_as_bound_arg`, `record_late_bound_vars`, `with`, `visit_ty`, and `visit_lifetime`.
Visits a poly trait ref using the general inner handler with non-lifetime binders allowed; it calls `visit_poly_trait_ref_inner`.
Visits an anonymous const under a late-boundary scope so late-bound regions cannot escape into constants. It calls `with` and `walk_anon_const`.

Resolves type and const generic parameters as references to themselves, then visits any default type, const type, or const default body attached to the parameter. It calls `resolve_type_ref`, `visit_ty`, `hir`, `body`, and `visit_body`.

Creates a nested `BoundVarContext` with a replacement scope and executes a callback inside that scope. It enters a debug span with `enter` and then invokes the provided closure `f`.
Stores the late-bound variable binder list for a HIR node in the output map and rejects accidental overwrites. It updates the map with `insert`.

Builds a binder scope where lifetime params may be early- or late-bound depending on `tcx.is_late_bound`, records the resulting late-bound binder kinds, and visits the nested item in that scope. It calls `record_late_bound_vars` to save binder info and `with` to traverse under the constructed `Scope::Binder`.

Builds a binder scope where all generic parameters are treated as early-bound, records that there are no late-bound vars, and then visits the nested item under both a binder scope and a trait-ref boundary. It calls `record_late_bound_vars` and uses `with` twice to install the scopes.

Resolves a lifetime reference by walking outward through the scope stack, tracking De Bruijn depth, root generics, binder entries, body ownership, and late-bound capture barriers to classify the reference as early-bound, late-bound, free, error, or unresolved. It uses `generics_of`, `param_def_id_to_index`, `get_generics`, and `shifted` while traversing scopes, and emits diagnostics through `feature_err`, `emit`, and `emit_err` when fresh/elided or improperly captured lifetimes are encountered.

Resolves a type or const generic parameter reference by walking outward through scopes, tracking binder depth and late-bound capture barriers, and classifying the reference as early-bound, late-bound, or unresolved/error. It uses `generics_of`, `param_def_id_to_index`, and `shifted` during lookup, and emits capture diagnostics with `emit_err` before recording the final result with `insert`.

Visits generic arguments on a path segment, resolving explicit lifetimes first, handling paren-sugar function traits specially, and computing object-lifetime-default scopes for type arguments based on the referenced item and surrounding context. It explicitly calls `visit_fn_like_elision` for paren-sugar segments, `visit_lifetime` for lifetime args, `object_lifetime_default` to compute defaults for type parameters, `with` to enter object-default scopes, `visit_ty` for type args, `visit_anon_const` for const args, `visit_id` for inferred args, and `supertrait_hrtb_vars` when collecting higher-ranked vars from supertraits.

Searches a trait/supertrait graph for an associated item with the given name and kind, accumulating higher-ranked bound variables introduced by traversed supertrait predicates. Resolves an elided object lifetime by scanning outward for the nearest applicable object-lifetime-default scope, adjusting for intervening binders, and defaulting to `'static` at the root. It calls `insert_lifetime` to record the chosen lifetime after applying `shifted`.
Records the resolved lifetime for a lifetime HIR node in the output map. It updates the definitions table with `insert`.

Removes a previously inserted lifetime mapping when later validation determines that the resolution was erroneous, asserting that the removed value matches the expected bad definition. It removes the entry with `swap_remove`.

Computes the set of lifetime parameters in a function owner that should be treated as late-bound by comparing where each lifetime appears in inputs, outputs, and where-clauses, while excluding lifetimes constrained through type aliases after lowering. Marks parameter types as constrained, skips descending into projection or inherent aliases, and otherwise continues recursive type traversal. It calls `kind` to inspect the type and `super_visit_with` to visit nested structure when traversal continues.
Ignores constants for constrained-argument collection and immediately continues traversal. It does not call other methods from the provided methods list.
Marks early-bound regions as constrained and otherwise leaves region handling unchanged. It calls `kind` to inspect the region kind.

Traverses HIR types to collect only those lifetime occurrences that contribute to input constraints, skipping associated type projections and selectively recursing into type-alias arguments based on a lowered-type constraint analysis. It calls the nested post-lowering visitor's `visit_ty`, visits constrained alias args with `visit_generic_arg`, traverses plain path segments with `visit_path_segment`, and falls back to `walk_ty` for ordinary recursive HIR traversal.
Collects named lifetime parameters encountered by the constrained-input visitor into its region set. It does not call any other methods from the methods list.
Collects every named lifetime parameter encountered during traversal into its region set. It does not call any other methods from the methods list.

Rejects late-bound type or const parameters in a binder, emitting either an immediate feature-gated error or a delayed bug, and rewrites their recorded resolution to `Error`. Looks up an associated type in a scope and then validates its accessibility and stability before returning it. It explicitly calls `lookup_assoc_ty_unchecked` and `check_assoc_ty`.
Performs raw associated-type lookup in definition order after identifier/scope adjustment, without checking visibility or stability. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Checks that an associated type is accessible from the current scope and stable at the use site, emitting and recording a privacy error when needed. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Finds accessible traits with an associated type of the requested name that also have some impl whose self type could match the queried type under inference. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Lowers a qualified associated type path into a projection type, or reports ambiguity when no self type is available by collecting plausible implementing types. It explicitly calls `ast_path_to_mono_trait_ref` and `create_args_for_associated_item`.

Rejects generic arguments and associated type bindings on path segments, builds a targeted diagnostic describing which kinds of generic arguments were supplied, and marks the context as tainted on error. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Reconstructs the definition/generic-argument meaning of each segment in a value path from the resolved endpoint, handling constructors, enum variants, trait items, and methods. It explicitly calls `probe_adt`.

Converts a resolved HIR path into a type by dispatching on the resolved definition kind, handling opaque types, ADTs, aliases, associated items, variants, and type parameters while also diagnosing misplaced generics and value-path misuse. It explicitly calls `prohibit_generics`, `ast_path_args_for_ty`, `ast_path_to_ty`, `def_ids_for_value_path_segments`, and `hir_id_to_bound_ty`.
Converts a HIR id resolved as a type parameter into the corresponding bound, early-bound, or error `Ty`. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Converts a HIR id resolved as a const parameter into the corresponding early-bound, late-bound, or error `Const`. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Public entry point for lowering a HIR type into `Ty` in normal context. It explicitly calls `ast_ty_to_ty_inner`.
Public entry point for lowering a HIR type into `Ty` when it appears inside a path. It explicitly calls `ast_ty_to_ty_inner`.

Validates that a delegated function signature uses only currently supported forms, rejecting recursive delegation, opaque outputs, early-bound generics, and unsupported ABI/safety/signature features. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Extracts the delegated input or output type from a callee signature, first rejecting unsupported delegation cases and then instantiating `Self` for impl methods when necessary. It explicitly calls `check_delegation_constraints`.

Main recursive HIR-type lowering routine that handles delegation inference, slices, pointers, references, tuples, anonymous ADTs, bare functions, trait objects, paths, opaques, and other type forms. It explicitly calls `ty_from_delegation`, `ast_ty_to_ty`, `ast_region_to_region`, and `res_to_ty`.

Builds the type representation for an `impl Trait`/opaque item by instantiating its generics, resolving supplied lifetime arguments, and returning either a projection in trait context or an opaque type otherwise. It explicitly calls `ast_region_to_region`.

Converts a function argument HIR type into a `Ty`. If the argument is `_` and an `expected_ty` is available, it records that inferred type via `record_ty` and returns it; otherwise it delegates to `ast_ty_to_ty`.

Builds a polymorphic function signature from HIR inputs/output, gathering late-bound variables, converting parameter and return types, and diagnosing disallowed `_` placeholders. It calls `tcx` to query signature/bound-var context, uses `suggest_trait_fn_ty_for_impl_fn_infer` to suggest trait method types for inferred impl method parameters/returns, converts each input with `ty_of_arg`, converts an explicit return type with `ast_ty_to_ty`, emits placeholder diagnostics and taints errors with `set_tainted_by_errors`, and finishes by checking region validity with `validate_late_bound_regions` before producing the bound fn sig.

When analyzing an impl method, looks up the corresponding trait method signature and extracts either the expected parameter type or return type to use as an inference suggestion. It calls `tcx` for HIR and trait-item lookup, converts the impl self type with `ast_ty_to_ty`, instantiates the implemented trait via `instantiate_mono_trait_ref`, and then reads the instantiated trait method signature to return the requested input or output type.

Checks that every late-bound region referenced in a signature is also constrained by the inputs. For each referenced region missing from `constrained_regions`, it creates an error with `generate_err`, adds extra notes for anonymous lifetimes that arise only through associated/opaque types, emits the diagnostic, and records the failure with `set_tainted_by_errors`.

Computes the lifetime bound for a trait object from its existential predicates when no explicit bound is given. It calls `tcx` and `object_region_bounds` to derive candidate regions, returns `None` if none exist, prefers `'static` when present, and otherwise returns the unique derived region; if multiple distinct regions are derived, it emits an ambiguity error and marks it via `set_tainted_by_errors`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ast_lowering/src/path.rs:: Lowers an AST path plus optional `QSelf` into an HIR `QPath`, using resolver `PartialRes` to split the resolved base from unresolved projections, handling async trait-bound remapping, and constructing either resolved or type-relative path forms. It calls `lower_ty` to lower the `QSelf` type, `lower_res` to convert the base resolution, `map_trait_to_async_trait` when an `async` bound targets an `Fn*` trait, `lower_path_segment` to lower every path segment with the appropriate generic-argument mode, `mark_span_with_reason` to tag desugared async-bound spans, `lower_span` for final HIR spans, and `next_id` when synthesizing type-relative HIR nodes.

Lowers an import path into `hir::UsePath`, preserving the provided per-namespace `Res` list and lowering each segment in a context where generic arguments are rejected. It calls `lower_path_segment` for each path segment and `lower_span` for the resulting path span.

Lowers one AST `PathSegment` into an HIR path segment by converting its identifier, resolution, and generic arguments, while diagnosing invalid parenthesized generics, return-type notation misuse, and missing angle brackets. It calls `lower_angle_bracketed_parameter_data` for `<...>` arguments, `lower_parenthesized_parameter_data` for `(...)` function-trait style arguments, `maybe_insert_elided_lifetimes_in_path` to synthesize omitted lifetime arguments when required, `lower_node_id`, `lower_ident`, and `lower_res` to finish the HIR segment, and uses resolver-backed `expect_full_res` to fetch the segment resolution.

Inserts synthesized elided lifetime generic arguments at the front of a path segment when the resolver recorded an elision anchor, choosing a diagnostic span based on whether brackets and other arguments are present. It calls `lower_lifetime` for each generated anonymous lifetime before wrapping them as lifetime generic arguments.

Lowers angle-bracketed generic arguments and associated-item constraints into an intermediate `GenericArgsCtor`, while also reporting whether the arguments are effectively elidable in optional-parameter mode. It calls `lower_generic_arg` for each non-constraint generic argument and `lower_assoc_item_constraint` for each associated-item constraint.

Lowers parenthesized function-trait-style generic arguments by turning inputs into a tuple argument and the return type into an `Output` associated type constraint, while enforcing the allowed `impl Trait` contexts and propagating async-bound feature tagging. It calls `lower_ty_direct` to lower input types, `lower_ty` to lower the return type under the correct `ImplTraitContext`, `ty_tup` to build tuple types for inputs or default unit output, `mark_span_with_reason` to tag desugared async-bound output spans, and `assoc_ty_binding` to create the synthetic `Output = ...` constraint.

Builds an HIR associated-type equality constraint like `Output = T` with empty generic arguments and fresh HIR identity data. It calls `next_id` to allocate the constraint HIR id and `lower_span` to lower the source span.

Maps the lang-item `Fn`, `FnMut`, or `FnOnce` trait `DefId` to its corresponding async function-trait lang item, returning `None` for all other traits. It does not call other methods from the listed methods set.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/check/wf: Returns the underlying `ObligationCtxt` by dereferencing `WfCheckingCtxt`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Returns the `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context inside the obligation context; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Normalizes a type-foldable value under the current parameter environment, attaching a `WellFormed` obligation cause for diagnostics; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Builds and registers a `WellFormed` predicate obligation for a generic argument using the current body and parameter environment. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`.

Creates the temporary inference/obligation context used for well-formedness checking, runs the supplied checker closure, solves obligations, computes implied bounds, lints redundant lifetimes, and resolves/report regions with a compatibility path for some implied-bounds cases; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Top-level dispatcher that selects the appropriate WF checker for the HIR node kind and then checks each generic parameter. It calls `check_item`, `check_trait_item`, `check_impl_item`, `check_foreign_item`, `check_item_type`, and `check_param_wf`.

Checks item-level well-formedness after precollecting item types, handling impls, functions, statics/consts/type aliases, ADTs, and traits according to item kind. It calls `check_impl`, `check_item_fn`, `check_item_type`, `check_type_defn`, and `check_trait`.
Checks a foreign item after precollecting its type information, validating foreign functions and statics while accepting foreign types unchanged. It calls `check_item_fn` and `check_item_type`.

Checks a trait item by precollecting its types, diagnosing misuse of the trait name as an unboxed self trait object, validating the associated item itself, and also validating synthesized associated types for RPITIT methods. It calls `check_dyn_incompatible_self_trait_by_name` and `check_associated_item`.

Analyzes generic associated types across all associated items of a trait to infer potentially missing outlives bounds by repeatedly intersecting constraints discovered from method signatures and other bounds. It calls `gather_gat_bounds`, `augment_param_env`, `region_known_to_outlive`, and `ty_known_to_outlive`.

Extends a parameter environment with additional clause predicates, returning the original environment unchanged when no new predicates are provided; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Collects GAT arguments appearing in a type/signature and derives required outlives clauses by checking whether referenced types or regions are known to outlive each region argument. It calls `GATArgsCollector::visit`, `ty_known_to_outlive`, and `region_known_to_outlive`.
Tests whether a type is known to outlive a region under the current environment by creating a region obligation probe. It calls `test_region_obligations`.
Tests whether one region is known to outlive another under the current environment by probing a subregion constraint. It calls `test_region_obligations`.

Creates a fresh inference context, applies a caller-provided set of region constraints, derives implied bounds from assumed well-formed types, and returns whether region solving succeeds without errors; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Constructs a `GATArgsCollector`, walks a type-foldable value, and returns the non-bound region and type arguments used at the target GAT projection. It calls `GATArgsCollector::visit_ty` indirectly through the visitor traversal.
Visitor hook that records lifetime and type arguments from projections of the targeted GAT, then continues recursively through nested types; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Returns whether a HIR type syntactically looks like a single-segment trait object naming the enclosing trait, indicating it may have meant `Self`; it does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Checks whether a trait item mistakenly refers to its own trait name where `Self` is intended, and emits a suggestion-based diagnostic when this makes the trait non-object-safe. It calls `could_be_self` to detect suspicious type references in associated const/type/function signatures and calls `is_object_safe` to skip diagnostics for object-safe traits.

Checks an impl item after precollecting its types, choosing an appropriate diagnostic span for methods and associated types before delegating to associated-item WF checking. It calls `check_associated_item`.

Checks generic-parameter well-formedness, focusing on const parameters: it either enforces the relevant lang-item trait bound in a WF context on feature-enabled paths or emits structural-match style diagnostics on stable paths. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt` and contains the local helper `ty_is_local`.
Local helper used by `check_param_wf` to decide whether a const-parameter type is local by recursively inspecting ADTs, arrays, slices, shared references, and tuples. It calls itself recursively.

Runs WF checking for an associated const, function, or type inside a dedicated context, ensuring trait coherence first, computing the appropriate `Self` type, and then validating the item-specific signature or value/type. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_associated_type_bounds`.

Checks structs, unions, and enums for representability and field/type well-formedness, enforces `Sized` where required for non-tail fields or packed/drop-sensitive layouts, registers extra obligations such as const evaluatability, and validates where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks a trait item by rejecting associated items on marker traits, validating the trait's where-clauses in a WF context, and then running the GAT missing-bound analysis for real traits. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `check_where_clauses`, and `check_gat_where_clauses`.

Validates explicit bounds on a trait associated type by normalizing each bound, expanding it into clause well-formedness obligations, and registering those obligations. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx` and `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`.
Checks a free or foreign function signature inside a dedicated WF context using the instantiated function signature. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`.

Checks the declared type of an item in a WF context by normalizing it, registering its well-formedness, optionally enforcing `Sized` depending on unsized-handling rules, and requiring `Sync` for eligible shared statics. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.

Checks an impl in a WF context by validating either the implemented trait reference and its derived obligations or the inherent self type, then validating the impl's where-clauses. It calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses`.

Checks where-clauses and generic defaults for well-formedness by registering obligations for concrete default types/consts, examining predicate dependencies, normalizing predicates, and feeding the resulting obligations into the current WF context. It calls `WfCheckingCtxt::tcx`, `WfCheckingCtxt::normalize`, and `WfCheckingCtxt::register_wf_obligation`.
Visits a type, records the index of any `ty::Param` encountered in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.
Stops traversal when a region is encountered by immediately returning `ControlFlow::Break(())`; it does not call other methods from the list.
Visits a const, records the index of any const generic parameter found in `self.params`, and then recursively continues traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.

Well-formedness-checks a function or method signature by liberating late-bound regions, normalizing each input/output type with per-parameter locations, registering WF obligations for every input/output type, and checking where-clauses. It explicitly calls `check_where_clauses` and uses `register_bound` to enforce the tuple and `Sized` requirements for `Abi::RustCall` arguments.

Validates a method's `self` receiver by normalizing the method signature, `self_ty`, and receiver type, then checking receiver legality. It explicitly calls `receiver_is_valid`, potentially multiple times under different feature configurations, to decide whether the receiver is accepted or which diagnostic to emit.

Emits error E0307 for an invalid `self` parameter type, adding an explanatory note and help text before returning the emitted diagnostic. It directly calls `dcx`, `with_note`, `with_help`, and `emit`.

Determines whether a method receiver type is valid for a given `Self` type by first trying direct type equality, then autodereferencing toward `self_ty`, registering autoderef obligations on success. When arbitrary self types are not enabled, it explicitly calls `receiver_is_implemented` at each deref step and also registers the corresponding `Receiver` bound before continuing.

Checks whether a candidate receiver type satisfies the `Receiver` lang-item trait by building the trait obligation and testing it with `predicate_must_hold_modulo_regions`; it does not call other methods from the list.

Checks that generic parameters of an ADT or lazy type alias are sufficiently constrained for variance computation, skipping items whose field/alias types already contain errors. It explicitly calls `identify_constrained_generic_params` to extend the constrained set and `report_bivariance` to emit diagnostics for unconstrained parameters.

Builds and emits the diagnostic for an unused/bivariant generic parameter, selecting item-specific help text and collecting spans where the parameter or `Self` alias appears. It explicitly calls `IsProbablyCyclical::visit_def` to detect likely recursive ADTs/type aliases so it can report recursive-usage diagnostics instead of plain unused-parameter errors.

Finds elaborated predicates on the current item that are globally true but nontrivial, normalizes them, refines their source span to the matching predicate clause when possible, and registers them as `TrivialBound` obligations. It does not call other methods from the provided list.

Runs well-formedness checking over all items, impl items, trait items, foreign items, and opaques in a module in parallel, combining their results, and checks for the crate entry function at the crate root. It explicitly calls `check_well_formed` for each covered definition.
Registers this module's query providers by installing `check_mod_type_wf` and `check_well_formed` into the compiler provider table. It explicitly references `check_mod_type_wf` from the methods list.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_builtin_macros/src/derivi: Entry point for `#[derive(Clone)]` expansion. It inspects the annotated item kind, checks whether the enclosing type also derives `Copy`, chooses between the optimized simple clone strategy and the general field-by-field strategy, configures bounds and attributes for the generated `Clone` impl, and invokes the generic derive framework to emit the impl. This method explicitly calls `has_derive_copy` to detect `Copy`, `combine_substructure` to wrap the chosen clone body builder, and then uses either `cs_clone_simple` or `cs_clone` as the method-body generator before finishing with `expand_ext`.

Builds the optimized `clone` body for simple cases, collecting assertion statements and returning `*self`. For non-union structs/enums it walks variant fields, deduplicates simple type names, and emits `AssertParamIsClone` checks; for unions it emits a single `AssertParamIsCopy<Self>` check instead. It explicitly calls `assert_ty_bounds` to generate these bound assertions.

Builds the general field-by-field `Clone` implementation by matching the derived substructure, reconstructing the original struct or enum variant, and cloning every field with explicit `Clone::clone` calls. It selects the appropriate constructor path from the matched shape and uses a local helper closure that calls `expr_call_global` on the standard `Clone::clone` path for each field.
Wraps the provided `CombineSubstructureFunc` in a `RefCell` so it can be mutably invoked later during derive expansion. Calls `RefCell::new`.
Constructs a `BlockOrExpr` containing only statements and no trailing expression.
Constructs a `BlockOrExpr` containing only a trailing expression, initializing the statement list with `ThinVec::new`.
Constructs a `BlockOrExpr` from an explicit statement list plus an optional trailing expression.
Converts the wrapper into an AST block, appending the stored trailing expression as a statement when present. Calls `cx.stmt_expr` and `cx.block`.

Converts the wrapper into an expression, returning the inner expression directly when possible and otherwise wrapping contents in a block expression. Calls `cx.block`, `ThinVec::new`, `cx.expr_block`, and `BlockOrExpr::into_block`.

Walks a type AST to collect occurrences of the derive target's type parameters together with any in-scope bound generic parameters, while rejecting macro calls inside the type. Calls the visitor entry `visit_ty` on the custom visitor, whose traversal in turn uses `visit::walk_ty`, `visit::walk_poly_trait_ref`, and emits `DeriveMacroCall` via `cx.dcx().emit_err` from `visit_mac_call`.

Checks whether a visited type node is a path naming one of the tracked type parameters, records it with the current bound-generic stack, and then continues recursive traversal. Calls `visit::walk_ty`.

Pushes bound generic parameters from a poly trait reference onto the stack for nested type collection, traverses the trait reference, then restores the previous stack length. Calls `visit::walk_poly_trait_ref`.
Rejects macro calls encountered while scanning types for derive bounds by emitting a `DeriveMacroCall` diagnostic. Calls `cx.dcx().emit_err`.
Entry point for deriving this trait on an item using the normal expansion path. Calls `TraitDef::expand_ext` with `from_scratch` set to `false`.

Dispatches derive expansion based on the annotated item's kind, detects `repr(packed)` on structs, expands structs and enums, reports unsupported unions, and pushes the generated item. Calls `attr::find_repr_attrs`, `TraitDef::expand_struct_def`, `TraitDef::expand_enum_def`, and `cx.dcx().emit_err` for union errors.

Builds the derived impl item, including the trait path, associated types, synthesized where-clause bounds over field types, and the final impl AST. Calls `self.path.to_path`, each associated type's `to_ty`, and `find_type_parameters` while constructing the where-clause and impl item.

Collects struct field types, generates each derived method body for the struct form, creates method items, and wraps everything in the final impl. Calls `MethodDef::extract_arg_details`, `MethodDef::is_static`, either `MethodDef::expand_static_struct_method_body` or `MethodDef::expand_struct_method_body`, then `MethodDef::create_method`, and finally `TraitDef::create_derived_impl`.

Collects field types from all enum variants, generates each derived method body for enum handling, creates method items, and wraps them in the final impl. Calls `MethodDef::extract_arg_details`, `MethodDef::is_static`, either `MethodDef::expand_static_enum_method_body` or `MethodDef::expand_enum_method_body`, then `MethodDef::create_method`, and finally `TraitDef::create_derived_impl`.

Packages the current derive context into a `Substructure` and invokes the user-supplied combine callback stored in `combine_substructure`. Calls `borrow_mut` on the `RefCell` and then invokes the callback.
Lowers the method's abstract return type description into an AST type for the current derive target. Calls `self.ret_ty.to_ty`.
Reports whether the derived method is static by checking that it has no explicit self parameter.

Separates method arguments into explicit self, self-like expressions, ordinary argument expressions, and their AST types for code generation. Calls `ty::get_explicit_self`, each argument type's `to_ty`, `cx.expr_ident`, `MethodDef::is_static`, and `cx.dcx().span_bug` for invalid non-return `Self` usage.

Constructs the final derived method AST item, including generics, parameters, return type, and body block. Calls `self.generics.to_generics`, `cx.param`, `MethodDef::get_ret_ty`, `cx.fn_decl`, and `BlockOrExpr::into_block`.

Builds the field view for a non-static struct derive method and forwards it to the combine callback as `SubstructureFields::Struct`. Calls `TraitDef::create_struct_field_access_fields` and `MethodDef::call_substructure_method`.
Builds the static summary for a struct and forwards it to the combine callback as `SubstructureFields::StaticStruct`. Calls `TraitDef::summarise_struct` and `MethodDef::call_substructure_method`.

Generates the body for a non-static enum derive method, handling zero-variant enums, fieldless-variant strategies, discriminant/tag comparisons, pattern construction, and per-variant field grouping before invoking the combine callback. Calls `TraitDef::get_tag_pieces`, `MethodDef::call_substructure_method`, `TraitDef::create_struct_pattern_fields`, and `TraitDef::create_struct_patterns`.

Builds static summaries for every enum variant and forwards them to the combine callback as `SubstructureFields::StaticEnum`. Calls `TraitDef::summarise_struct` for each variant and `MethodDef::call_substructure_method`.

Summarizes a struct or variant's field layout into named, unnamed, or empty `StaticFields`, preserving the derive span context and rejecting mixed named/unnamed layouts. Calls `cx.dcx().span_bug` on invalid mixed-field input.

Constructs pattern ASTs for matching a struct or variant for each provided prefix, creating bindings for every field and choosing struct, tuple-struct, or unit patterns by shape. Calls `TraitDef::mk_pattern_ident` and emits `cx.dcx().span_bug` if a struct-form field unexpectedly lacks an identifier.

Shared helper that turns each field of a struct/variant into a `FieldInfo` by asking a closure to build expressions for all self-like arguments, then splitting out the first as `self_expr`. Calls the supplied `mk_exprs` closure.
Creates a field-binding identifier of the form `{prefix}_{i}` for generated match patterns. Calls `Ident::from_str_and_span`.

Builds `FieldInfo` values backed by pattern-bound field identifiers for each self-like argument prefix. Calls `TraitDef::create_fields` and, inside its closure, `TraitDef::mk_pattern_ident`, `cx.path_ident`, and `cx.expr_path`.

Builds `FieldInfo` values by generating direct field-access expressions from each self-like argument, with special handling for packed structs to avoid creating unaligned references. Calls `TraitDef::create_fields` and, inside its closure, uses AST-building helpers such as `cx.expr`, `cx.expr_block`, `cx.block`, `cx.stmt_expr`, and `cx.expr_addr_of`.

Builds a fold expression over the current `SubstructureFields`, delegating each step to the supplied callback `f`. For `EnumMatching` and `Struct`, it checks `is_empty`, selects the initial field with `split_first` or `split_last`, creates per-field expressions via `f`, and combines them by iterating with `iter` plus `fold` or `rfold`. For `EnumTag`, it calls `f` for the tag test and optionally combines it with the provided match expression. For unsupported static or fieldless forms, it terminates with `dcx().span_bug()`.
Registers collect-phase query providers into `Providers` and delegates to `resolve_bound_vars::provide` to install bound-variable related queries before filling this file’s query entries.
Records the span of inferred placeholder types (`_`) encountered in a type node, then calls `intravisit::walk_ty` to continue traversing nested type structure.

Checks generic arguments for inferred placeholders, recording their spans; for inferred args it calls `intravisit::walk_inf`, and for type args it explicitly calls `visit_ty` to reuse type placeholder handling.
Records the span of inferred array lengths and then calls `intravisit::walk_array_len` to visit nested array-length structure.

Emits a placeholder-type diagnostic for item signatures when any placeholder spans were collected; if spans exist, it calls `placeholder_type_error_diag` and then emits the returned diagnostic with `.emit()`.

Builds the detailed diagnostic for illegal placeholder types in item signatures, including generic-parameter replacement suggestions and special handling for bare functions in const/static contexts. It calls `bad_placeholder` to create the base diagnostic and may call `tcx.parent_hir_node` and `multipart_suggestion` when forming suggestions.

Rejects placeholder types in supported item signatures by selecting the item’s generics/suggestion mode, visiting the item with `HirPlaceholderCollector::visit_item`, and then calling `placeholder_type_error` with the collected spans.
Returns the HIR map from `self.tcx.hir()` for nested visitor traversal.

For each item, forces signature-level lowering by calling `lower_item`, checks item signatures for placeholder types via `reject_placeholder_type_signatures_in_item`, and then calls `intravisit::walk_item` to recurse into nested HIR.

Ensures type information for generic parameter defaults is collected: it calls `self.tcx.ensure().type_of` for type defaults and const parameters, calls `self.tcx.ensure().const_param_default` for const defaults, and finally calls `intravisit::walk_generics` to continue traversal.

When encountering a closure expression, forces collection of closure generics and codegen attributes by calling `self.tcx.ensure().generics_of` and `self.tcx.ensure().codegen_fn_attrs`, then calls `intravisit::walk_expr` to visit nested expressions.
Forces lowering of each trait item by calling `lower_trait_item`, then calls `intravisit::walk_trait_item` to traverse inside the trait item.
Forces lowering of each impl item by calling `lower_impl_item`, then calls `intravisit::walk_impl_item` to traverse inside the impl item.
Creates the base diagnostic for placeholder types in item signatures by pluralizing the item kind, sorting spans, and calling `tcx.dcx().create_err` with the placeholder error payload.
Constructs a new `ItemCtxt` with the given type context and item `LocalDefId`, initializing error taint tracking to empty.
Lowers an HIR type into a rustc `Ty` by calling `astconv` and then `ast_ty_to_ty`.
Returns the HIR id for the current item by calling `self.tcx.local_def_id_to_hir_id(self.item_def_id)`.
Fetches the current HIR node for this item by calling `self.hir_id()` and then `self.tcx.hir_node(...)`.
Reports whether this item context has already been marked with an error by calling `self.tainted_by_errors.get()` and converting the stored state into `Result`.
Returns the underlying type context stored in the item context; it does not call other listed methods.
Returns the current item as a global `DefId` by calling `to_def_id` on the local item id.
Fetches generic predicates for an associated type parameter at a span by calling `at` and then `type_param_predicates` on `tcx`.
Disables region inference in item collection by always returning `None`; it does not call other listed methods.
Reports that placeholder type inference is not allowed during this collection phase by always returning `false`; it does not call other listed methods.
Creates an error type for an illegal placeholder type by calling `tcx` and `new_error_with_message`.
Creates an error constant for an illegal placeholder const after normalizing regions by calling `fold_regions`, `tcx`, and `new_error_with_message`.
